clue.text: Popular chap I invited out and bullied

parts.note: popular things are 'in', fashionable
Tim is a man's name, standing for any chap
to invite someone out for a romantic evening is to date them, so invited out gives dated

explanation.surface: A popular man asked someone on a date and then pushed them around.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bullied has been frightened into submission, which is what being cowed or threatened means.

clue.text: Drive mischief-maker over English lake

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed over the others sits above them, so it comes first

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous sprite
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A troublemaker drives someone over an English lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive someone to act is to push or urge them forward, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Keen worker at bottom of ditch

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece at the bottom of another is written after it

parts.note: a trench is a long ditch
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: An eager labourer digging at the bottom of a ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen here means sharp or incisive, as a cutting remark is, the sense of a penetrating comment.

clue.text: Tiny child receiving letter in Greece

indicators.note: receiving means the word for child takes another piece inside it

parts.note: a mite is a small child
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A small child getting a letter while on holiday in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean extremely small; the adjective is stressed on its second syllable.

clue.text: Appreciate archaeologists' undertaking

definitions.meaning: slang for liking or appreciating it

explanation.surface: Valuing the work that archaeologists do.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang verb for enjoying something, and the noun for an excavation site project.

clue.text: Walks unsteadily, beginning to track river creatures

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken from the word track

parts.note: otters are aquatic mammals living by rivers

explanation.surface: Someone staggers about at the start of their attempt to follow some river wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to stagger or wobble while moving on foot.

clue.text: Plan mattered awfully, like some stores

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly mangled and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A plan mattered a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Large shops divided into sections are called department stores, so they are of that kind.

clue.text: Away working in sort of club, excelling

parts.note: someone away is out, not at home
a performer at a strip club works by stripping

explanation.surface: A cryptic picture of someone out on the town, working in a club and doing brilliantly.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip rivals is to surpass or outdo them, so this is excelling over them.

clue.text: In court, youngster takes in many at first — very many!

indicators.note: takes in means one piece swallows another inside it

parts.note: someone up before the magistrate is in court, so up means appearing in court

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word many

parts.note: a teen is a teenager, a youngster

explanation.surface: A young person appearing in court admits to a very large number of offences.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'up' before the magistrate is to be in court, a British idiom; 'takes in' and 'at first' work on the first 'many', while the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for an indefinitely large number, a great many.

clue.text: Start the day in distinctive clothing?

definitions.meaning: to rise from bed in the morning
an outfit, especially an eye-catching or odd one

explanation.surface: Getting dressed in eye-catching clothes first thing in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means rising in the morning; the hyphenated noun means a costume or striking outfit.

clue.text: Lawyer thus allowed into bar at last

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
licit means lawful, allowed

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of each of the words into and bar

explanation.surface: A lawyer is finally admitted to the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into bar' looks like a barrister being called; it is just the source of the last letters O and R.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain this is a lawyer who advises clients and prepares cases, distinct from a barrister.

clue.text: Pragmatic about girl's nervous affliction

parts.note: re means about, concerning
Ali is a girl's name, so the girl's gives Ali's
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: Being practical about a girl's nervous twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A pragmatic person is sensible and practical, facing things as they really are.

clue.text: Organ used in Baroque arias

indicators.note: used in signals letters sitting within the following words

explanation.surface: An organ playing in some Baroque arias.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' looks like the musical instrument of the Baroque scene; it is the body organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of hearing, one of the body's sense organs.

clue.text: Further showing of broadcast about fuel

parts.note: re means about, concerning
peat is dug and burned as fuel

explanation.surface: A programme about fuel is shown again.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun of a television programme is a second airing of it.

clue.text: Loot obtained by convict breaking into stately home

indicators.note: breaking into means one piece goes inside another, as a burglar enters a house

parts.note: a pile is a large grand house
an old lag is a convict

explanation.surface: Stolen goods taken by a convict who burgled a stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, both mean to plunder or ransack a place.

clue.text: Old cab, reportedly well-proportioned

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is heard said, a word that sounds alike

parts.note: something handsome is well-formed and well-proportioned

explanation.surface: A shapely vintage taxi, by all accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage for hire, common in Victorian London.

clue.text: More affected holiday-maker

definitions.meaning: camp means theatrically affected, so its comparative means more so
someone on holiday in a tent

explanation.surface: A rather theatrical tourist.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of the adjective for showy or mannered, and a person on holiday in a tent or van.

clue.text: Friend knocking drink back

indicators.note: back means the word for drink is read from the end to the start

parts.note: to lap is to drink, as a cat does

explanation.surface: A mate downing a drink in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back' looks like one idiom for drinking; 'knocking' is just a link and 'back' turns LAP round.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a mate or companion.

clue.text: Deportation excludes ex — it's the custom

indicators.note: excludes means the following letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: extradition is the deportation of someone to face trial abroad
taken as written

explanation.surface: Banning former partners from deportation is the done thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom is a long-established practice handed down, an inherited way of doing things.

clue.text: Daughter misses meal — it's part of the target

indicators.note: misses means the letter is left out

parts.note: dinner is a meal
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter skips dinner; that is part of the plan.
explanation.definitionFit: On an archery or darts target, the ring just outside the bull is called by this word.

clue.text: Improper to take forty winks in it

indicators.note: in places the sleep inside the following word

parts.note: forty winks is a short sleep, a nap

explanation.surface: It is not done to have a snooze on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsuitable or inappropriate, as a remark that does not fit the occasion.

clue.text: Heavyweight initially training cricket side

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of the word training

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A heavyweight begins training with a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of weight, so anything that weighs one is heavy indeed.

clue.text: Flowering plant, one carried by teacher's favourite girl

parts.note: the teacher's pet is a favoured pupil

indicators.note: carried by means the one is held within the girl

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A flowering plant brought in by the class favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden annual with trumpet-shaped flowers, a member of the nightshade family.

clue.text: Politician introducing more obese-sounding tradesman

parts.note: a Green is a member of the Green Party; this politician is introducing, or leading off, what follows

indicators.note: -sounding means a word that sounds like the following letters

parts.note: grosser means fatter, more obese

explanation.surface: A politician presents a shopkeeper who seems fatter.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper selling fruit and vegetables is a kind of tradesman.
